introduction:
A Death Certificate in Andhra Pradesh is issued by the local Municipality, Gram Panchayat, or Grama/Ward Sachivalayam under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969. It is the official legal proof of death and records the name, date, place, and cause of death.

The certificate is essential for claiming insurance, settling bank accounts, property mutation, pension claims, and legal succession proceedings. Registration is primarily managed through the unified AP Seva system (Grama/Ward Sachivalayams) and the national CRS portal (crsorgi.gov.in).
quickFacts:
Important to Know
  • Hospital vs Home Deaths: If a death occurs in a hospital (Institutional), the hospital administration is legally responsible for reporting it directly to the CRS portal. The family does not need to register it. If the death occurs at home (Non-Institutional), the head of household must report it within 21 days.
  • AP Seva Integration: While MeeSeva is still valid, the AP government has integrated services into the AP Seva Portal. Citizens are directed to their local Grama/Ward Volunteer or Secretariat (Sachivalayam) rather than private MeeSeva centers.
  • First certified copy is FREE; subsequent copies are available for a nominal fee.
  • Registration between 21 days and 1 year requires written permission from the Registrar + late fee. Beyond 1 year, a Magistrate/RDO order is required.
documentsRequired:
Documents Required for Death Certificate

Note: Submit self-attested photocopies and carry original documents for verification.
Proof of Death
  • Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD) from hospital (for hospital deaths)
  • Burial/Cremation ground receipt or certificate from local authority/elder (for home deaths)
  • FIR or Panchnama copy (only for unnatural or accidental deaths)
Identity Proof of Deceased
  • Aadhaar Card (Mandatory if available)
  • Voter ID / Ration Card
  • PAN Card / Passport
Informant & Witness Details
  • Aadhaar Card of informant (head of household or close relative reporting the death)
  • Relationship proof with deceased
  • Two witness identity proofs (for home deaths)
For Delayed Registration (>1 Year)
  • Non-Availability Certificate (NAC): Issued by the registrar after a formal search of the CRS database reveals no existing death record for that year.
  • Order from the Sub-Divisional Magistrate / Revenue Divisional Officer (RDO).
  • Self-affidavit on stamp paper.
onlineApplication:
Method 1: Download/Register Online via CRS & AP Seva

How you proceed online depends entirely on where the death occurred:

Case A: Hospital (Institutional) Death — Print Certificate
  1. Do Not Register From Scratch: The hospital administration will report the death directly to the CRS Portal. Trying to register this manually online will create a duplicate entry rejection.
  2. Wait & Search: Wait 3 to 5 working days for the hospital to upload the details. Go to the CRS National Portal or AP Seva Portal.
  3. Download: Search using the deceased's name, date of death, gender, and hospital name to download the digitally signed certificate directly.
Case B: Home (Non-Institutional) Death — New Registration
  1. Visit Portal: Log in to the AP Seva Portal.
  2. Select Service: Select "Health & Revenue Services" → "New Death Registration (Home)".
  3. Fill Details: Input the deceased's name, date of death, address, informant's Aadhaar, and upload the local cremation/burial slip or affidavit.
  4. Submit: Pay the online service charge (~₹35) and download the acknowledgment slip with the Reference Number.
offlineApplication:
Method 2: Offline Process at Grama/Ward Sachivalayam or MeeSeva

Offline registration is heavily integrated with the local secretariat network:

Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Determine Location & Contact Volunteer: Contact your Grama/Ward Volunteer or visit the nearest Grama/Ward Sachivalayam (Secretariat Office).
  2. Hospital Death: If the death occurred in a hospital, take the hospital death slip/discharge card directly to the Sachivalayam digital assistant. They will print the pre-registered certificate for you.
  3. Home Death Registration: Request the offline Death Registration Form. Fill in the deceased's details, date/place of death, and informant Aadhaar information.
  4. Submit Checklist: Submit the filled form with the cremation/burial receipt and Aadhaar copies. Pay the service charge (approx. ₹35) to the operator.
  5. Local Verification & Release: The Village Revenue Officer (VRO) will verify the details. Once approved by the local registrar/Tahsildar, the certificate is issued.
afterApplying:
After Applying — Validation & Delayed Cases

Track & Download

Track status using the Reference/Application ID on the AP Seva Portal or search directly on the CRS National Portal.

Institutional Deaths Availability

Ensure you get the hospital reference slip. Do not attempt a manual entry online for hospital deaths.

Delayed Registration (How to Get NAC)

If the death registration is delayed by more than 1 year, you must obtain a Non-Availability Certificate (NAC). To do this, submit a formal search request on the CRS database via AP Seva. Once the Registrar searches the records for that specific year and verifies that no record exists, they will issue the NAC. This NAC is a mandatory prerequisite to apply to the RDO/Magistrate for a late registration order.
